title: Buddy's daring harmonic playing
summary: Buddy came home from the army so advanced and bold that local musicians were wary, and he pushed Wes harder than Wes pushed him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: It got to be, were leaps and bounds of how he was improving so much with his sound and his touch. Confident. I wasn't into music, I wasn't even knowing exactly what he was doing, but it wasn't hard to tell, it was quite a...he was advancing.

I remember when Buddy came home, Wes and I was playing around town, sometime together, sometime not, depending on who came up with a job and called. And we'd run in, then, whatever...Buddy came home and everybody was scared of him -- musicians. Not the fear, physical, you know, but...
Just that he was now such a good player that...

Not only that, Buddy was kind of a quiet, withdrawn ...and you never knew what he was thinking. It was almost like he has a whole different way. He was so...But it was strong, it was really strong. It was like, when he played something -- and Bud wasn't afraid to go out. I mean, Bud wasn't a fixed player; he didn't play out of a box. Bud played what he heard, the music was to him. He played what the music was to him. It wasn't the same thing I would have played, or what you would have played, or somebody else would have played. It's what Buddy would play. And he was so far advanced from the average one, his playing was so far advanced that you wouldn't question him.
You mean musically more advanced than Wes, for instance?
I wouldn't say musically in terms of experience and all that, but...
Were his harmonic concepts more daring, or...?

Yeah, that's exactly what it was. Much more. Because I heard Wes and Buddy sit down and play where they were practicing, I mean where they were rehearsing for something, or just playing on the gig, and they were challenging one another. I mean really challenging one another. And Buddy kept Wes in more trouble than Wes kept Buddy. Chasing, chasing after whatever. Buddy was playing some...Buddy would go in someplace with changes and he'd take him out somewhere and you don't know where you're at with the changes. So guys like...
Or how to get back. But he always did, so nobody would say anything about, 'Hey, that ain't right.'
Well, that must have been a challenge for all three of you, to play together.

Not only all three of us, but everybody in town. All the guys, when Buddy come round, when Buddy was playing, they would really...Buddy was so much advanced and bold. He wasn't afraid of...like a guy would know how you can go into certain cycles and come out; and when you go in, you come out over here. But Buddy would come out and come 'way back out there somewhere.

But he had a way no matter where he came from with it, he had a thing...he had a kind of gifted thing. He could just hear; he could just...it would just resolve, just like it was just a simple thing, somebody writing "Tea for Two."
